key_dates.note: Beats EPS by 5.77%; EquipmentShare (3.5% ABR) alleged fraud

thesis_points: Acquisition flywheel: relationship-driven bilateral sourcing → 8.16% cap rate, 18.7yr WALT, 2.2% annual bumps → 10.0% GAAP yield vs peers' 7–8%
88% of H1 2025 deployments came from existing tenants — tenant-growth pipeline, not cyclical opportunism
Tenant risk is overpriced: ZIPS bankruptcy was a balance-sheet failure, not demand destruction; car wash same-store sales resilient through recessions
Portfolio: 2,261 properties, 48 states, 99% occupancy, 51% Sunbelt ABR, 400+ tenants (no one >4% ABR), 3.4x rent coverage
Revenue: 77.6% service-based (car washes, medical/dental, childcare, QSR) — insulated from e-commerce disruption

overview.narrative:
REITs posted a broadly positive session on May 26, with hospitality leading all subsectors at +2.69% on renewed travel demand optimism heading into the summer season. Park Hotels (PK) topped the tape at +4.26%, while office names surprised to the upside with a +1.44% average gain, led by Hudson Pacific (HPP, +3.83%). Retail and industrial posted solid mid-1% gains. At the bottom, housing (-0.24%) and towers (-0.02%) were the only subsectors in the red, dragged by Sun Communities (SUI, -2.25%) and SBA Communications (SBAC, -1.87%).

The intra-sector dispersion is notable. Within towers, Uniti (UNIT, +2.08%) and SBAC (-1.87%) diverged nearly 400bps, suggesting company-specific catalysts rather than macro rotation. Similarly, healthcare showed a wide 305bp spread between CareTrust (CTRE, +1.99%) and Strawberry Fields (STRW, -1.06%). The weakness in manufactured housing names SUI and ELS (-1.72%) amid broader REIT strength bears monitoring — rate sensitivity or park-level fundamentals may be souring sentiment in that pocket.

Positioning into tomorrow, the risk-on tone favoring cyclical property types — hospitality, office, retail — suggests the market is pricing in a more constructive economic backdrop. We would lean into hospitality momentum while trimming manufactured housing exposure. Watch whether office can sustain follow-through above this +1.4% move or fades back to its defensive range.
